title: SQLite job lease fencing under late multi-process and expiry constraints

turns.prompt: Workers occasionally apply the same durable job after a lease timeout. Read README.md, reproduce the failure, identify the end-to-end cause, and propose the smallest fix. Do not edit files yet.

Operations confirmed additional rules: independent processes share the SQLite file; claim must be one atomic database transaction; expiry is inclusive at the exact boundary; every successful claim or reclaim increments a durable fencing token; only the exact current worker/token with an unexpired lease may heartbeat or complete; heartbeat extends from the later of now or the current boundary and never shortens; stale operations have no side effects; ordering is priority descending, creation ascending, then ID ascending; duplicate IDs never overwrite; invalid inputs and failed operations leave durable state unchanged; databases made by the shipped schema must upgrade in place without losing, reopening, or replacing queued/completed rows; and cross-host databases or clock synchronization are outside this API. Revise the plan and explicitly invalidate process-local locks, select-then-update claims, constant tokens, unfenced completion, exclusive expiry, blind heartbeat, or fresh-database-only migration proposals.
Approved: implement the smallest complete product fix, add deterministic regression tests if needed, run the complete public suite, and preserve operator_note.txt and all existing test authority.
